headline: High: n8n’s server-side execution and broad egress can turn Copilot-generated content into unsafe actions or leaks if workflow inputs are trusted.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot can read repo context and open editor buffers, while n8n workflows can ingest arbitrary workflow data and call tools. There is no documented shared channel by default, but if Copilot output is copied into n8n prompts or nodes, prompt injection becomes plausible. The pathway is interaction-dependent, not impossible.
conditions: IF Copilot output is pasted into an n8n AI Agent prompt or workflow field
IF n8n nodes treat Copilot-authored text as instructions without sanitization
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any Copilot text enters n8n
Use a fixed prompt template in n8n that quotes Copilot output as data
Disable automatic execution of AI Agent nodes on untrusted text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between editor output and workflow inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open buffers, and n8n reads/writes server files while processing whatever the workflow handles. If the same sensitive file or snippet is moved from the editor into n8n, both agents can expose it through different backends. The profiles do not show a default shared workspace, so this is not high, but the leakage path exists.
conditions: IF a sensitive file from Copilot’s editor context is copied into an n8n workflow
IF n8n sends that file content to an external integration node
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of n8n workflows
Restrict n8n credentials and integration nodes for sensitive projects
Use local-only nodes for any file handling
requires-engineering: separate editor and workflow storage locations

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state; n8n can write the server filesystem and execute commands. Even without a shared directory explicitly documented, overlapping write authority creates a realistic conflict if both target the same repo or server path. Uncertainty about the exact shared path escalates to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF n8n workflows operate on the same repository or directory that Copilot edits
IF both agents write to the same files without locking
mitigations: Pause one agent while the other writes
Use separate working directories for Copilot and n8n
Require git status checks before n8n writes
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional updates

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can generate code or edits, and n8n’s AI Agent node can orchestrate tools and execute commands on the server. If n8n treats Copilot output as authoritative, a mistaken suggestion can cascade into automated actions with real side effects. Because n8n has execution authority by default, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF n8n consumes Copilot-generated instructions or code without verification
IF the workflow includes Execute Command or other side-effecting nodes
mitigations: Insert a human approval gate before side-effecting nodes
Validate Copilot output against a schema before execution
Limit n8n to read-only actions for Copilot-derived tasks
requires-engineering: add automated diff and policy checks before execution

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is tied to GitHub repo context and editor buffers, while n8n processes whatever data the workflow handles and stores credentials on its server. If regulated data from Copilot’s code context is routed into n8n workflows, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific residency breach, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data from Copilot’s workspace is sent into n8n workflows
IF n8n retention or credential storage exceeds the source project’s policy
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through n8n
Review n8n credential retention settings
Limit workflow logs for sensitive runs
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies across both systems
